title: What is recognition of prior learning?
description: Recognition of prior learning (RPL) assesses existing skills and experience for credit towards a qualification. How it works, evidence rules, an example.
shortAnswer: A recognition of prior learning (RPL) assessment is the process of assessing the skills and knowledge a person has already gained, through formal study, work or life experience, against the requirements of a qualification or unit, and granting credit for what they can prove. Qualification frameworks such as Australia's treat RPL as an assessment that must meet the same standard as any other assessment.
keyTakeaways: The AQF defines RPL as an assessment process covering formal, informal and non-formal learning to determine credit outcomes.
RPL is an assessment, not an exemption: evidence must be valid, sufficient, authentic and current.
Under the 2025 Standards for RTOs, Standard 1.6 requires providers to offer RPL and make decisions in line with their assessment system.
Credit transfer is different: it recognises completed equivalent units or qualifications without reassessing the person.

sections.heading: How is recognition of prior learning defined?

blocks.text: Many national qualification systems recognise prior learning. The Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF) is a well documented example: its [glossary](https://www.aqf.edu.au/publication/aqf-glossary) defines RPL as "an assessment process that involves assessment of an individual's relevant prior learning (including formal, informal and non-formal learning) to determine the credit outcomes of an individual application for credit." Credit, in the same glossary, reduces the amount of learning required to achieve a qualification.

The Australian Qualifications Framework Council's [explanation of RPL](https://www.aqf.edu.au/download/425/recognition-prior-learning/19/recognition-prior-learning/pdf) says RPL assessment should be the same standard as other assessment for the qualification, should recognise learning regardless of how, when and where it was acquired, and must ensure evidence is valid, authentic, current and sufficient.

sections.heading: How does the RPL process work?

blocks.text: The RPL process works by matching a person's evidence to the requirements of a unit or qualification, testing that evidence, and filling any gaps with training. The AQF explanation lists typical stages:

items: Advise the applicant about the process.
Give the applicant enough information to prepare evidence to the required standard.
Assess using appropriate evidence gathering methods and tools.
Report to internal and external stakeholders.

blocks.text: Methods named in the AQF explanation include mapping prior learning outcomes to the qualification components, oral or written questioning, observation in work based or simulated settings, challenge assessments and third party reports or work products.

sections.heading: What do Australia's 2025 Standards for RTOs require for RPL?

blocks.text: Standard 1.6 of the 2025 Standards for RTOs requires registered training organisations to offer RPL, base decisions on evidence under their assessment system, and document decisions fairly, transparently and consistently. The Australian Skills Quality Authority (ASQA) [RPL and credit transfer practice guide](https://www.asqa.gov.au/for-providers/standards-for-RTOs/practice-guides/quality-area-1-training-and-assessment/RPL-and-credit-transfer-practice-guide) expects RPL to be applied "with the same rigour" as other assessment and to meet the principles of assessment and rules of evidence in Standard 1.4.

ASQA lists known risks, including promoting RPL as an easy, quick or guaranteed path to a qualification, failing to verify that evidence is authentic, not testing evidence for currency, and automatically granting RPL to someone who holds a higher AQF level qualification in the same industry. Standard 1.7 separately covers credit transfer. The wider requirements are summarised in [Standards for RTOs 2025: training and assessment](/regulations/standards-for-rtos-2025-training-and-assessment).

sections.heading: How is RPL different from credit transfer and verification of competency?

blocks.text: RPL is one of the defining features of [competency-based training](/glossary/competency-based-training): because the standard, not the time spent, is what matters, evidence gained anywhere can count.

sections.heading: What does an RPL application look like?

blocks.text: Illustrative example: an experienced aged care worker without a formal qualification applies for RPL.

items: **Mapping:** the assessor maps the worker's duties statement and training records against each unit's performance and knowledge evidence.
**Evidence:** supervisor reports, a portfolio of de-identified care plans and a workplace observation.
**Testing:** a competency conversation probes knowledge gaps; the assessor checks that evidence is recent and the worker's own.
**Outcome:** RPL granted for most units; gap training and assessment for two units where evidence was insufficient.
**Record:** the mapping, evidence, questions and decision are retained with the same rigour as any assessment.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Because Knowledge Foundry holds each program as a framework of competencies and assessment points, prior evidence can be mapped to specific points rather than to whole courses. Only the unmet points need training, and each credit decision keeps a traceable record.

faqs.q: Is RPL easier than doing the course?
faqs.a: It should not be. RPL removes unnecessary training, not assessment. ASQA identifies promoting RPL as an easy, quick or guaranteed path to a qualification as a known risk to quality outcomes, and expects RPL to meet the same principles of assessment and rules of evidence as other assessment.

faqs.q: What counts as evidence for RPL?
faqs.a: Anything that validly shows current skills and knowledge against the unit requirements: work samples, position descriptions, supervisor or third party reports, licences, previous training records, observation and questioning. Evidence must be authentic and current, and overseas evidence may need mapping to local legislative requirements such as work health and safety laws.

faqs.q: Can a workplace use RPL for internal training?
faqs.a: Yes, in principle. An employer can recognise existing competence against its own competency framework and skip training that is not needed. The result is not nationally recognised unless it is assessed by a registered training organisation against a nationally endorsed unit, but the same evidence principles make the decision defensible.

faqs.q: Does RPL apply in higher education?
faqs.a: Yes. The AQF definition applies across all sectors, and universities and other higher education providers grant credit or advanced standing on the basis of prior learning. Each provider sets its own policy and must maintain the integrity of qualification outcomes.
